html:
Ambohimanga is a fortified royal village on a hill north of Antananarivo, the seat of the Merina kings in the 18th century and the most sacred site of the highlands, listed by UNESCO in 2001.

Here Andrianampoinimerina began the reunification of Imerina. Its walls, gates closed by great stone discs, royal tombs and wooden palace were kept as a holy place after the capital moved to Antananarivo.

Under Ranavalona I Christians and foreigners were barred from it. The French moved the royal relics to Antananarivo in 1897 to break its power, but people still come to pray to the royal ancestors, a tradition close to the turning of the bones.
sum: Ambohimanga is a fortified royal village on a hill north of Antananarivo, the seat of the Merina kings in the 18th century and the most sacred site of the highlands, listed by UNESCO in 2001.
